s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic eruption with skin lesions and liver dysfunction
salient_findings: Pruritic eruption that began on the trunk and spread to all extremities
Scleral icterus and multiple dusky, thin plaques with a central collarette of scale
Hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles with a greenish-black hue on hands and feet
key_facts: Eruption began on the trunk and spread to all extremities
Denied contact allergens, fever, or hyperhidrosis
No prior history of atopic dermatitis, dermatophytosis, or hand eczema
Punch biopsy of the right palm revealed psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis and intraepidermal spongiosis

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rosea
shortlist.why_kept: Punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with pityriasis rosea

shortlist.label: Porphyria cutanea tarda
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic eruption with skin lesions and liver dysfunction, elevated bilirubin levels

shortlist.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
shortlist.why_kept: Liver dysfunction with elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin levels

shortlist.label: Alcoholic liver disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of alcoholic cirrhosis and elevated liver enzymes

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Punch biopsy of the right palm revealed psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a pruritic eruption with dusky, thin plaques and hyperkeratotic plaques, along with the laboratory findings of elevated bilirubin and liver enzymes, and the presence of amorphous pink material in the eccrine duct on biopsy, are consistent with porphyria cutanea tarda, especially in the context of alcoholic cirrhosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rosea
rejected.why: While punch biopsies of the chest and thigh were consistent with pityriasis rosea, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not support this as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Primary biliary cirrhosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the vignette to support a diagnosis of primary biliary cirrhosis, such as antimitochondrial antibodies or a characteristic liver biopsy.

rejected.label: Alcoholic liver disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, this diagnosis does not directly explain the cutaneous findings.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: The presence of psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis on biopsy is not sufficient to diagnose psoriasis, given the other clinical and laboratory findings that point towards a different diagnosis.
